extracted.intended_audience: citizens and voters of New York / the American public considering ratification of the Constitution
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for assessing the merits, structure, and republican character of a proposed national constitution, emphasizing tradeoffs among stability, energy, and liberty and the need for clear partitions of authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive critical examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine clearly and fully the merits of this Constitution by taking a more critical and thorough survey of the work of the convention: examine it on all its sides, compare it in all its parts, and calculate its probable effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ultimate object is to judge the Constitution’s merits and the expediency of adopting it; this requires a complete, comparative, and forward-looking review rather than cursory or partisan commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation and impartiality in judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Public measures should be investigated with a spirit of moderation essential to a just estimate of their tendency to advance or obstruct the public good; avoid predisposition to censure or predetermination to condemn or applaud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers and critics should avoid partisan bias — neither predetermined patrons nor predetermined adversaries provide reliable judgments. The papers address those with sincere zeal for public happiness and a temper favorable to just estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for human fallibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that a faultless plan was not to be expected and allow for errors chargeable to the fallibility of the convention as a body of men; critics themselves ought not to assume infallibility in rejudging the fallible opinions of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make allowances for errors arising from the limited human faculties and the novelty/complexity of the undertaking rather than demanding perfection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance energy, stability, and liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: A crucial difficulty is combining the requisite stability and energy in government with the inviolable attention due to liberty and the republican form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three are essential: energy for security and law enforcement; stability for national character and confidence; liberty requires powers derived from the people and safeguards like short durations and plural hands. The constitution must mix these in due proportion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy in government
rubrics_metrics.description: Energy in government is essential to that security against external and internal danger, and to that prompt and salutary execution of the laws which enter into the very definition of good government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Energy generally requires a certain duration of power and the execution of it by a single hand; without it the government cannot effectively respond to dangers or enforce laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability in government
rubrics_metrics.description: Stability in government is essential to national character and to the advantages annexed to it, as well as to that repose and confidence in the minds of the people, which are among the chief blessings of civil society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stability favors continuity of officeholders; frequent changes produce frequent changes in measures and disquiet; people expect remedies for vicissitudes and uncertainties of state administrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republican liberty requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The genius of republican liberty seems to demand that all power should be derived from the people, that those intrusted with it should be kept in dependence on the people by a short duration of their appointments, and that even during this short period the trust should be placed not in a few, but a number of hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle creates tension with stability and energy; constitutional design must reconcile short terms and plural officeholders with the needs of energetic and stable governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper partition between general and State governments
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark the proper line of partition between the authority of the general and that of the State governments; this is an inherently difficult task because boundaries among authorities are subtle and often indeterminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the obscurity arising from complex objects, imperfect human faculties, and inexact language — expect compromises and some sacrifice of theoretical neatness to practical exigency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and precision of language
rubrics_metrics.description: Perspicuity requires not only that the ideas should be distinctly formed, but that they should be expressed by words distinctly and exclusively appropriate to them; no language is so copious as to supply words for every complex idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguity in constitutional text is inevitable to some degree, but careful drafting and attention to the vehicle of expression lessen obscurity; complex and novel provisions deserve particular linguistic care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and compromise between large and small states
rubrics_metrics.description: The larger and smaller states have interfering pretensions; compromises on representation and organization of government were necessary and likely required sacrifices of theoretical propriety to secure union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate arrangements in light of political realities and the need to unify diverse states; expect bargaining that alters idealized constitutional symmetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of factional contamination in framing
rubrics_metrics.description: The convention’s proceedings were unusually exempt, it is suggested, from the pestilential influence of party animosities; deputies were induced to sacrifice private opinions and partial interests to the public good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A constitution framed with minimal factional bias and with delegates willing to compromise is more worthy of confidence than one produced by narrow partisan designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative improvement over the Confederation
rubrics_metrics.description: A new constitution need not be perfect; it is sufficient that it is an improvement over the existing Confederation on important practical points (e.g., powers to raise money/troops, mixture of powers, bill of rights, treaty power, limits on slave importation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the proposed constitution relative to the defects of the existing system; many objections to the new plan are tenfold weight against the Confederation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective powers commensurate to objects
rubrics_metrics.description: A government which does not possess regular powers commensurate to its objects is exposed to dissolution or usurpation; declaring powers necessary and rendering them nugatory is folly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional grants should be capable of practical execution; avoid rendering essential powers impotent, which invites extra-constitutional usurpation or overreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary multiplication of experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Great imprudence is shown in unnecessarily multiplying experiments in government; frequent and needless constitutional tinkering is hazardous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prudence favors adopting a workable government now rather than perpetually delaying for a hypothetically better model that may never be agreed upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a republic
rubrics_metrics.description: A republic may be defined as a government which derives all its powers directly or indirectly from the great body of the people, and is administered by persons holding their offices during pleasure, for a limited period, or during good behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this functional definition as the principal test of whether the form and aspect of the plan are strictly republican; if the plan departs from this character it should be rejected.
